newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Hewlett bucks market trend, falls.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Hewlett bucks market trend, falls.

text.p: Put options on shares of Hewlett-Packard Co were active on Friday as the stock bucked a strong market trend and traded lower.
In late trading, the stock was down two at 43-1/4 on heavy turnover of 8.9 million shares. It hit a session low of 42-1/2.
Traders said concern about the company's earnings, which are not due until mid-November, could have been the reason for the stock's decline, which took place in the face of a broad market advance.
The Dow was ahead 51 points at around 5,984.
Among the Hewlett options, the October 45 put traded 4,270 contracts, the October 42-1/2 put traded about 3,100 and the October 40 put traded 2,770.
With the stock down below the 45 strike price, the October 45 put was up 15/16 at 2-1/4. Its open interest was 3,100.
On the call side, the October 45 call traded nearly 5,300 contracts. It was down 13/16 at 3/4. Its open interest was around 4,800.
"The stock's looked awful here for a few days," a trader on the CBOE said. "I would suspect they're worried about the earnings."
"There's been a lot of put buyers," he added.
Elsewhere, large-size spreads in options on Cisco Systems crossed on the CBOE while the stock surged 2-3/8 to 67. Turnover was 5.4 million shares.
The Cisco October 65 call, up 15/16 at 2-13/16, traded an even 12,000 contracts, 10,000 of which was from block spreads of 5,000 contracts each.
The Cisco October 60 call traded more than 10,400 contracts. It rose 1-7/8 to 7-1/4. Open interest was nearly 17,000 contracts.
Of the volume, 7,675 contracts were done as a spread.
Technology stocks once again took the spotlight, with issues including Motorola Inc, Micron Technology and Compaq Computer joining Hewlett and Cisco on the leader board.
On the American Stock Exchange, a couple of spreads were seen in long-dated options on Office Depot.
The Office Depot January 1997 20 call traded 5,800 contracts and the January 25 call traded 5,300 contracts.
Two blocks, one of 3,000 contracts and one of 2,000 contracts, crossed in both the January 20 and 25 calls. --Gregory Crawford, 312-408-8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com
